results.title: Hypergraph Neural Network
results.content: * Hypergraph Neural Network (HGNN) is a neural architecture that extends graph neural networks by modeling high-order interactions using hyperedges connecting arbitrary subsets of nodes. Attention mechanisms assign variable weights to hyperedges and/or their member nodes during message passing: αi,e​=softmax(aT[Wxi​∥Wxe​]) This enables HGNNs to learn the relative importance of different high-order relations in a data-driven fashion, supporting multiple attention heads and semantic diversity (Yang et al., 11 Mar 2025, Srinivas et al., 2024, Jin et al., 7 May 2025). Hypergraph autoencoders (HGAE/VHGAE), GANs (HGGAN), and diffusion models (HGGDM) extend hypergraph modeling to unsupervised, generative, and temporal learning (Yang et al., 11 Mar 2025). Heterogeneous hypergraph models (MGA-HHN) employ multi-granular attention across meta-path–defined views for fine-grained node and hyperedge semantics (Jin et al., 7 May 2025). * **Knowledge hypergraph representation**: Hyperbolic HGNNs with hyper-star message passing preserve multi-relational and positional semantics, improving node classification and link prediction (Li et al., 2024).
